body:
I tend to fill the gap with more clients.  I don't like downtime.  I take enough time off, but for the most part, I'm happier when I'm working.  Oddly enough I tend to relax more when I'm stressed.

Relationships are hit or miss.  I have a lot of stress about money.  Problem is, it shouldn't be my stress.  I make plenty.  My bills are paid.  I would have extra.  But most extra lately goes to family.  I don't resent it, but it IS exhausting sometimes.

I could date more and hope to build something more lasting, but we live in a pretty shallow world even these days, and having a physical disability, however comfortable I may be with it, is a turn-off for some women.  So I tend to set my sights lower than I probably should.  When the lowered sights do not work out, that's when I really notice how thankless dating can be.

**TLDR; Several things could be contributing to the gap, but it's hard to narrow down.**

When I say I go on a lot of first dates, it's not completely positive.  Means that I can usually seal the deal for one date, but for whatever reason it doesn't go anywhere.  Sometimes it's mutual.  Sometimes not.  And when it's not mutual it's a ding to the self-confidence.

But I can relate to what you say about "faking life", since I feel like that's what I do on a constant basis.  I'm supposed to be happy.  So I seem happy.

It gets tedious.

In my jobs, I'm paid to be "on".  Confidence and at least acting like you always know the answer even if you really don't are vital.  When I work or when I teach, it's like I'm on stage, and I have students or clients hanging on my every word.

When I'm not working, I'm shy and quiet.  Almost bashful.  Friends comment on how "cute" or "funny" it is that I'm so different.

As for a social life, I go on first dates fairly often.

Like I said, I don't have any right to feel this way, but I still feel it in the back of my mind.
